title: Iterated Hom differential calculation on a localized pure tensor
statement: Let C be a site, R a sheaf of commutative rings and K,L,M cochain complexes of R-modules. Let n,t,p,q be integers with p+q=t. Use the degreewise comparison a_n and product projections pi of the Hom complexes [lem-sc-hom-tensor-degreewise, def-pur-hom-complex], and T=Tot(K tensor L) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a section s of homComplex(K,homComplex(L,M))^n over U, a localized object W→U and sections x of K^p and y of L^q over W, evaluate at sigma(x tensor y) the two internal Hom sections obtained from s by (d_iterated;a_(n+1);pi_(n+1,t);internalHom(iota,id)) and by (a_n;pi_(n,t);internalHom(iota,d_M)) - (-1)^n(a_n;pi_(n,t+1);internalHom(d1,id)) - (-1)^n(a_n;pi_(n,t+1);internalHom(d2,id)). Their scalar values in M^(t+n+1)(W) agree. Here iota is the (p,q) summand inclusion, sigma is the canonical presheaf tensor-to-sheaf tensor map, and d1,d2 are the first and signed second tensor summand differentials. No equality on arbitrary sheaf tensor sections is asserted.

source.place: Lemma sites-cohomology-lemma-compose (Tag 0A90), differential calculation of More on Algebra Lemma more-algebra-lemma-compose (Tag 0A5Y)

proof.text: Apply the degree-(n+1) curry equation to d_iterated(s). Expand the outer Hom differential projection using lem-sc-hom-complex-projections at degrees p,p+n,p+n+1,p+1, then evaluate on x. Its postcomposition is the inner Hom differential on f(x); its precomposition is -(-1)^n f(d_K(x)). Expand the inner Hom differential at L^q to get d_M(f(x)(y))-(-1)^(p+n)f(x)(d_L(y)), with the outer precomposition term still -(-1)^n f(d_K(x))(y).

By the definitions of the two tensor summand differentials and naturality of sigma, d1 sends sigma(x tensor y) to the (p+1,q) inclusion of sigma(d_K(x) tensor y), while d2 sends it to (-1)^p times the (p,q+1) inclusion of sigma(x tensor d_L(y)). Apply the degree-n curry condition to identify the three right-side scalar values. Use Int.negOnePow_add, scalar associativity, and commutativity of multiplication of integer units to identify the signs. The two subtraction terms commute in the target additive group. These calculations also hold in negative degrees and when any section or differential vanishes.

theorem homTensorDifferential_summand_pure
    (K L M : CochainComplex Mod ℤ) (n t p q : ℤ) (h : p + q = t) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory R
    let T := CochainComplex.mapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod)
    let ι := CochainComplex.ιMapBifunctor K L (curriedTensor Mod) p q t h
    let f :=
      (homComplex (R := R) K (homComplex (R := R) L M)).d n (n + 1) ≫
        homTensorDegreewiseMap R K L M (n + 1) ≫
          homTensorProjection R T M (n + 1) t (t + (n + 1)) rfl ≫
            SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) ι (𝟙 (M.X (t + (n + 1))))
    let g :=
      (homTensorDegreewiseMap R K L M n ≫
        homTensorProjection R T M n t (t + n) rfl ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) ι (M.d (t + n) (t + (n + 1)))) -
      n.negOnePow • (homTensorDegreewiseMap R K L M n ≫
        homTensorProjection R T M n (t + 1) (t + (n + 1)) (by omega) ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R)
            (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.d₁ K L (curriedTensor Mod)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p q (t + 1)) (𝟙 (M.X (t + (n + 1))))) -
      n.negOnePow • (homTensorDegreewiseMap R K L M n ≫
        homTensorProjection R T M n (t + 1) (t + (n + 1)) (by omega) ≫
          SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R)
            (HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.d₂ K L (curriedTensor Mod)
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ) p q (t + 1)) (𝟙 (M.X (t + (n + 1)))))
    ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ)
      (s : (homComplex (R := R) K (homComplex (R := R) L M)).X n |>.val.obj U)
      (W : (Over U.unop)ᵒᵖ) (x : (K.X p).val.obj (op W.unop.left))
      (y : (L.X q).val.obj (op W.unop.left)),
      (((f.val.app U).hom s).app W).hom
        (((homTensorSectionMap R (K.X p) (L.X q)).app (op W.unop.left)).hom
          (x ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj (op W.unop.left)] y)) =
      (((g.val.app U).hom s).app W).hom
        (((homTensorSectionMap R (K.X p) (L.X q)).app (op W.unop.left)).hom
          (x ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj (op W.unop.left)] y))
